body.statement: Every law satisfying existential rank similarity has a rank-invariant replacement with one \(V\sim\operatorname{Unif}[0,1]\) and potential outcomes \((Q_0(V),Q_1(V))\) that preserves \(\mathcal L(Y_d\mid U)\) for \(d\in\{0,1\}\), the observed law \(q\), and every policy mean on \(p^{1:L}\).
body.justification: This reduction turns existential conditional rank equality into a single ordered support without imposing an independent probability-integral-transform jitter.
body.gap: Marx uses rank similarity for sharp policy bounds, but the finite-alphabet joint construction with missing complier support is not stated as this replacement lemma.
body.consumer: The common rank makes joint policy compatibility enumerable by finitely many chains.
